jordana: quick probe — I ran a small bring-up for the new int8 reranker with candidate priming + left-padding enabled. seeing a subtle NDCG dip on short queries, wondering if priming tokens are being counted in kv-cache/prefix lengths incorrectly.

 tanner: hmm ok. what numbers?

 jordana: baseline fp16 NDCG@10 0.842, int8 without priming 0.838, int8 with priming+pad 0.815. MRR also down ~0.02. small sample (10k queries) but consistent across two seeds.

 eva: that delta is larger than expected. could be tokenization offsets — priming adds soft tokens and we may be truncating doc context vs candidate differently when padding is applied.

 sam: do we have the exact batching config? are we bucketing by total tokens or by doc length?

 jordana: bucketing by total tokens, batch_size=64, max_seq=512, pad_strategy=left. code used: ```python
# generate inputs
inputs = tokenizer(priming + query + candidate, truncation=True, max_length=512, padding='longest')
```

 tanner: left-pad + kvcache + continuous batching can shift kv cache positions if we reuse offsets incorrectly. also quantized kernels sometimes assume clean attention masks.

 eva: can you dump a minimal reproducer for a single query -> two candidates showing token ids + attention mask + kv offsets? if priming tokens are on the left and we pack, the candidate tokens might land at different indices between fp16 and int8 runtime because of micro-batching order.

 jordana: +1. I pushed a tiny repro to the test bucket: `s3://redwood-tests/priming-padding/repro-5108765432.tar.gz` includes token dumps and our run command.

 sam: also check if we accidentally applied prefix caching earlier in the pipeline for int8 path only (there was that optimization for repeated prefixes). could introduce stale prefix lengths.

 jordana: good catch — I grep'd the runtime logs, see `apply_prefix_cache=True` in the int8 run but not in fp16. ops-bot logged an automated optimization toggle during the deploy.

 ops-bot: deploy-opt-toggle: prefix_cache optimized for model-rank-2 on 2024-10-03T14:22:11Z by infra-ops.

 tanner: that explains a lot. if prefix_cache is applied, priming is effectively double-counted for some batches. try a controlled run: int8 + priming but prefix_cache=False, and also swap to right-padding to see if bucket alignment fixes it.

 jordana: running both now. ETA ~30m for small smoke. will post numbers.

 eva: also add a small eval that strips priming from the tokenization (i.e., run candidate+query only) to measure exact priming effect. if priming improves rank in fp16 but harms int8 then it's a kernel/runtime issue, not an eval shift.

 sam: if this reproduces, plan: 1) disable prefix_cache for int8 until kernel fix; 2) add a unit test that compares token positions across quantized vs fp16 for primed inputs; 3) run a larger 100k query job.

 jordana: results from smoke: int8+priming+prefix_cache=True -> NDCG@10 0.814 (confirm). int8+priming+prefix_cache=False -> 0.836. right-padding + prefix_cache=False -> 0.839 (almost parity).

 tanner: excellent — looks like prefix_cache interaction with left-padding + quantized path. small weekend patch then.

 eva: action items for tomorrow: patch runtime to ignore prefix_cache when left-padding or when padding changes between candidates, add CI check, and rerun 100k job.

 jordana: I'll open the PR and include the reproducer + logs. thanks team. :thumbsup:

 sam: thanks — can you tag me on the PR? I'll help with the kernel repro.

 jordana: tagging you now in #code-review.

 ops-bot: ci-pipeline: rerank-smoke (5108765432) queued for run on linux-x86-intel-rt.
